verdict.line: You lose if you let her stack A Thousand Cuts procs uncontested past level 6; you win if you force all-ins before she hits that spike.

brief.thesis: Gnar vs Gwen is a tempo race decided by range and form state. Mini Gnar's Q (Boomerang Throw) outranges her entire kit at 1100 units, so you can poke safely while she's stuck closing distance with E (Skip 'n Slash, 400 range). The problem is the 39.2% win rate over 51 games: once she lands E and stacks on-hit magic damage, her sustain from A Thousand Cuts snowballs trades she wins outright, and your Mega Gnar transform timing becomes the only reset button you have.

tell.watch: Your Rage bar / her E cooldown

theirWindow.what: She dashes in, gains attack speed and magic on-hit, and if she connects the cooldown partially refunds. This is her all-in button — if she dashes onto you expect a full extended trade, not a poke.

yourWindow.when: Her E on cooldown AND you're Mega Gnar
yourWindow.what: Walk up and use Q (Boulder Toss) to hit and slow, then E (Crunch) to land for area damage. Without Skip 'n Slash she has no gap closer and no attack speed steroid, so she cannot trade back.

powerCurve.note: Mini Gnar Q range dominates her Q cone
E unlocked both sides, trades sharpen
Her R adds poke, E refund snowballs
On-hit items widen her sustain lead

start.why: Taken in 74.3% of games (46.2% win over 52) — the extra sustain and damage matter because you need to win short trades before her E refund loop starts.

boots.why: 63.2% pick rate (48.8% win) — the magic resist directly blunts A Thousand Cuts and her R slow duration.

core.why: First item in the most common path — the move speed and on-hit damage let Mini Gnar kite her E dash instead of eating it.
Second in every listed path — armor shred helps Mega Gnar's E (Crunch) and R (GNAR!) burst her down before she stacks healing.
Tied for third pick (18.8%/9.4% combos) — the HP and damage reduction counter her sustain-through-damage passive directly.

situational.when: she builds heavy attack speed on-hit and out-sustains your trades
you need the magic resist and on-hit damage to match her scaling
the game goes long and you need flat damage reduction in teamfights

runes.keystoneWhy: Taken in 33.9% of games (36.4% win) — the heal-on-hit from kiting pokes offsets her A Thousand Cuts sustain in extended trades. Master-tier players (1,803 games) instead run Lethal Tempo, which suits a more aggressive Gnar who wants to win attack-speed trades at range rather than disengage-and-reset.

summoners.why: Run in 64.6% of games (50% win) — Teleport lets you reset after losing a trade to her E refund loop without forfeiting wave or tempo elsewhere on the map.

playing.title: Poke before her E is up
playing.detail: Use mini Gnar's Q (Boomerang Throw, 1100 range) whenever her E (Skip 'n Slash) is on its 13-11s cooldown. She cannot punish you from outside 400 range.

playing.title: Never fight into her W
playing.detail: W (Hallowed Mist) makes her untargetable to anyone outside it. Do not walk into the mist to auto her — you'll eat free damage while she takes none.

playing.title: Time your transform to her E cooldown
playing.detail: Rage builds from combat; try to hit max Rage and transform into Mega Gnar right as her Skip 'n Slash goes on cooldown so she has no dash to escape your E (Crunch).

playing.title: Track her Q snip count
playing.detail: Snip Snip! fires up to 6 times and deals true damage with A Thousand Cuts procs in its center. Don't stand in the center cone repeatedly — the true damage ignores your resists.

playing.title: Save R for a wall stun
playing.detail: GNAR! only stuns and adds bonus damage to enemies who hit a wall. Position Gwen against lane terrain before casting, otherwise it's just a slow.

playing.title: Don't contest extended all-ins past level 6
playing.detail: Her solo-kill advantage comes from R (Needlework) poke plus A Thousand Cuts healing compounding in long fights. Take short trades, back off before stacks build.

playing.title: Catch your Q boomerang
playing.detail: Catching Boomerang Throw reduces its cooldown — this is how you keep outranging her E window after window. Missing the catch means a full 16-10s wait depending on rank.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and summoner spells above are measured from live games on the current patch (16.20.1) via OP.GG; the tactical reasoning connecting them to ability mechanics and timings is my own analysis, not sourced data.
